title: Lesson 16 · Advanced Analysis
blurb: Ellipsis, simple vs complete subject, simple vs complete predicate, and sentence analysis.

items.prompt:
Which word is understood (left out)?

“Shut the door.”
items.explain: A command has the understood subject “you”: [You] shut the door.

items.prompt:
Which word is understood (left out)?

“He is older than I ___.”
items.explain: The comparison drops the verb: older than I [am].

items.prompt:
Which word is understood (left out)?

“Run home!”
items.explain: A command has the understood subject “you”: [You] run home.

items.prompt:
What is the simple subject (the bare subject word)?

“A great storm is raging.”
items.explain: The bare subject is “storm” (drop the modifiers “A great”).

items.prompt: The bare subject word, without modifiers, is called the ___.
items.explain: The bare subject word is the simple (grammatical) subject.

items.prompt: The subject with all its modifiers is called the ___.
items.explain: The subject plus its modifiers is the complete (logical) subject.

items.prompt: The bare verb, without modifiers, is called the ___.
items.explain: The bare verb is the simple (grammatical) predicate.

items.prompt:
What is the complete subject?

“A great storm is raging.”
items.explain: The subject with its modifiers is “a great storm.”

items.prompt:
What is the complete predicate?

“The storm rages furiously.”
items.explain: The verb with its modifiers is “rages furiously.”

items.prompt: What is ellipsis?
items.explain: Ellipsis is the leaving out of words that are understood.

items.prompt:
What is the complete subject?

“The little boy ran home.”
items.explain: The subject with its modifiers is “The little boy.”

items.prompt:
What is the complete predicate?

“Birds sing sweetly.”
items.explain: The verb with its modifiers is “sing sweetly.”

items.prompt:
What is the complete subject?

“My old friend writes letters.”
items.explain: The subject with its modifiers is “My old friend.”

items.prompt:
What is the complete predicate?

“The tired soldiers marched slowly.”
items.explain: The verb with its modifiers is “marched slowly.”

items.prompt: Abridgment shortens a complex sentence by turning a clause into a ___.
items.explain: Abridgment turns a subordinate clause into a phrase or a single word.
